headline: GOLD FIRMS TO $4,128 AS OIL SURGE REVIVES DECEMBER FED RISK; SILVER SLIDES 1.0% TO $58.63
snippet: Gold edged up 0.45% to $4,128.20/oz on October 8 as an oil price spike revived inflation concerns and rekindled the case for a December Fed rate hike, pulling silver down 1.04% to $58.63 amid a stronger US dollar and weak equity futures. Dow e-mini futures were down 462 points, underlining a risk-off tone that kept gold bid while weighing on silver's industrial demand component.

headline: HOT CHILI GROWS LA VERDE: 112M @ 0.47% CUEQ FROM 42M DEPTH — BROAD PORPHYRY BUILDS TOWARD RESOURCE
source_name: Mining Stock Education / Hot Chili (ASX/TSXV: HCH)
snippet: Hot Chili (ASX/TSXV: HCH) added another wide copper-gold intercept at its La Verde discovery in Chile's Atacama region, with RC hole DKP067 returning 112 metres grading 0.47% CuEq (0.40% Cu, 0.10 g/t Au) from 42 metres depth. La Verde has now produced multiple holes exceeding 100m of copper mineralisation from surface, building toward a maiden resource estimate for a porphyry system whose previous best returned 391m at 0.51% CuEq.

headline: GOOGLE LOCKS IN 3,590 MW OF CONSTELLATION NUCLEAR POWER — AI DATA CENTRE DEMAND NOW BACKSTOPS URANIUM BULL CASE
snippet: Alphabet signed a 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity from Constellation reactor uprates, plus a 15-year deal for 2,700 MW of existing Constellation generation — the largest single corporate clean power commitment on record at US$4.3 billion in planned upgrades. Constellation gained 14%, Vistra rose 10%, Talen 11%, and uranium miners rallied broadly as AI data centre demand for firm carbon-free power is now structurally underwriting the nuclear investment case.

headline: RARE EARTH TRADE THESIS UNRAVELS ON US-CHINA THAW: USA RARE EARTH, MP MATERIALS EACH FALL 5%
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) and MP Materials (MP) each fell roughly 5% on October 7 as diplomatic warming between Washington and Beijing quietly dismantled the supply-chain trade thesis — with Critical Metals (CRML) declining 3% in sympathy. The selloff underlines how much of the sector's 2026 premium was priced on geopolitical tension rather than operating fundamentals, raising questions about how much upside remains if export restrictions ease.

headline: ANGLO CEO: TECK MEGA-MERGER AND CHINA NICKEL SALE ARE 'TEST CASES FOR GEOPOLITICAL DEAL-MAKING'
snippet: Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad said the pending US$54 billion Anglo-Teck copper merger — awaiting only Chinese regulatory sign-off — and the sale of Brazilian nickel assets to China's MMG represent a new model for mega-deals that must satisfy both Western investors and Chinese supply chain priorities simultaneously. The EU has extended its Phase II review of the MMG nickel deal on European steelmaker supply security grounds while every other regulator has cleared Anglo-Teck.

headline: RPX GOLD EXTENDS HIGH-GRADE WAWA CORE WITHIN PEA PIT: 25.50 G/T AU OVER 4.26M INCLUDING 135 G/T OVER 0.71M
snippet: RPX Gold (TSXV: RPX) extended high-grade gold mineralisation within the open pit outlined in its 2026 Preliminary Economic Assessment at the Wawa Gold Project in Ontario, with a drill intercept of 25.50 g/t gold over 4.26 metres including a 135.00 g/t Ag lens over 0.71 metres. Pre-Feasibility Study drilling is expected to conclude by late October, targeting a resource upgrade ahead of the PFS completion.

headline: EQUITY METALS SILVER QUEEN: 310 G/T SILVER AND 2.6 G/T GOLD OVER 2.6M — Q4 VALIDATION CONFIRMS NO. 3 VEIN CONTINUITY
source_name: Investing News Network / Equity Metals (TSXV: EQTY)
snippet: Equity Metals (TSXV: EQTY) released assays from 17 validation holes totalling 5,719 metres at Silver Queen in British Columbia, with highlight hole SQ26-171 returning 2.6 metres averaging 2.6 g/t gold and 310 g/t silver alongside copper, lead and zinc credits. The Q4 program is designed to validate resource continuity on the No. 3 Vein ahead of a planned resource update and feasibility decision.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM RESTARTS GROTA DO CIRILO UNDER TAC SETTLEMENT — APPEALS COURT LIFTS EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
snippet: A Brazilian appeals court lifted the emergency injunction that had shuttered Sigma Lithium's Grota do Cirilo complex, enabling an immediate restart under a Terms for Adjustment of Procedures (TAC) agreement with the state of Minas Gerais that includes US$540,000 in environmental fines. Benchmark Minerals had flagged the shutdown as a near-term spodumene supply constraint given Grota do Cirilo's 330,000-tonne annual concentrate capacity.

headline: STEWART THOMSON: GDX MONTHLY BULL FLAG TARGETS $170–$200 — $4,200–$3,941 GOLD RANGE IS THE BUY ZONE
snippet: Veteran precious metals commentator Stewart Thomson argues the October 2026 gold pullback has produced a textbook monthly bull flag on the GDX chart, with a measured move target of $170–$200 per share — implying roughly 2x–2.5x from current levels. Thomson frames the $4,200–$3,941/oz gold range as the tactical buy zone for both the metal and mining equities, noting that major breakouts historically consolidate 6–18 months before the next trending leg.

headline: OROGEN ROYALTIES CREATES CIBOLA COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY ROYALTY IN BC — NORTHERN DISCOVERY METALS TAKES PROJECT
snippet: Orogen Royalties (TSXV: OGN) structured a royalty deal on its Cibola copper-gold porphyry project in British Columbia, with Northern Discovery Metals (CSE: NOR) acquiring a 100% interest while Orogen retains a royalty. The transaction converts an exploration-stage BC porphyry into royalty revenue for Orogen without further capital outlay, following the company's strategy of spinning its greenfield assets into royalties.
